problem: "a fibre at distance y from the neutral axis has length proportional to y" is wrong: in a straight beam every fibre between two sections has the same original length. What varies with y is the change in length, and hence the strain.
fix: "In a straight beam, the change in length of a fibre — and therefore its strain — is proportional to its distance y from the neutral axis, so stress is linear in y."

where: Section 1, sentence after the stress formula
problem: Typo "r = Ri n" — the stray n makes the sentence read as a product Ri × n.
fix: "At the inner fibre, r = Ri, so the term (Rn − r) is positive and largest there."

where: Section 1, formula block for Rn and e
problem: The symbol b appears in A = b h without ever being defined. Depth h, Ri and Ro are defined; the width is not.
fix: Add to the symbol list: "b is the width of the rectangular section (mm); h is the depth (mm); A = b h is the area (mm²)."

problem: "the horizontal section through the hook where the load line passes near the centre of curvature" is garbled: the load line is taken to pass through the centre of curvature, so it cannot pass "near" it, and it does not identify which horizontal section is critical.
fix: "The critical section is the horizontal section whose inner fibre lies closest to the load line — that is, the section with the smallest centroidal radius R. There the load line is at distance R from the centroid, so M = P R."

problem: Both plotted curves include the direct stress P/A (the +11.111 term), but the axis is labelled simply "stress (MPa)" and the curves are named "curved" and "straight". The chapter defines σ as bending stress only, so a student may take the curve as bending stress alone (the inner value would then read about 110 MPa, not 121 MPa).
fix: Label the y-axis "total stress σtotal = P/A + σ (MPa)" and say in the caption that both lines are the total stress at the inner and outer fibres.
